The Red Heifer — Balaam — The Second Census — Inheritance Law — The Journey's End

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

Governed by the Bamidbar Book-Level Critical Apparatus (v1.2) — full manuscript census, evidence hierarchy, and bibliography maintained there

4Q27 (4QNumb) — major expansionist, pre-Samaritan-type witness, DJD XII ed. Jastram

4Q23 (4QLev-Numa) — DJD XII, ed. Ulrich

4Q121 (4QLXXNumb) — Greek LXX Numbers

Samaritan Pentateuch — 4QNumb shares major interpolations with SP at named locations

Ketef Hinnom silver amulets — oldest physical witness to any biblical text (Num 6:24–26)

Part One (Chapters 1–18) is frozen and separate; this volume covers Chapters 19–36 only

COMPARATIVE NOTES AT END OF EVERY CHAPTER

DSS  ·  MASORETIC VARIANT  ·  CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitutions

All personal names in original Hebrew form throughout

BAMIDBAR — CHAPTER 19 The Ashes of the Red Heifer

19:1 And YHWH spoke to Moshe and to Aharon, saying:

19:2 This is the statute of the law which YHWH has commanded, saying: Speak to the children of Yisra'el, that they bring you a red heifer, faultless, wherein is no blemish, and upon which never came a yoke.

19:3 And you shall give her to Elazar the priest, and she shall be brought forth outside the camp, and she shall be slain before his face.

19:4 And Elazar the priest shall take of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood toward the front of the tent of meeting seven times.

19:5 And the heifer shall be burnt in his sight; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her dung, shall be burnt.

19:6 And the priest shall take cedar-wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

19:7 Then the priest shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he may come into the camp, and the priest shall be unclean until the evening.

19:8 And he that burns her shall wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and shall be unclean until the evening.

19:9 And a man that is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside the camp in a clean place, and it shall be kept for the congregation of the children of Yisra'el for a water of sprinkling; it is a purification from sin.

19:10 And he that gathers the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening; and it shall be to the children of Yisra'el, and to the stranger that sojourns among them, for a statute for ever.

19:11 He that touches the dead, even any man's dead body, shall be unclean seven days;

19:12 the same shall purify himself therewith on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean; but if he purify not himself the third day and the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

19:13 Whoever touches the dead, even the body of any man that is dead, and does not purify himself -- he has defiled the tabernacle of YHWH -- that soul shall be cut off from Yisra'el; because the water of sprinkling was not dashed against him, he shall be unclean; his uncleanness is yet upon him.

19:14 This is the law: when a man dies in a tent, every one that comes into the tent, and every thing that is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.

19:15 And every open vessel, which has no covering close-bound upon it, is unclean.

19:16 And whoever in the open field touches one that is slain with a sword, or one that dies of himself, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.

19:17 And for the unclean they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the purification from sin, and running water shall be put to it in a vessel.

19:18 And a clean person shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle it upon the tent, and upon all the vessels, and upon the persons that were there, and upon him that touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave.

19:19 And the clean person shall sprinkle upon the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he shall purify him; and he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in water, and shall be clean at evening.

19:20 But the man that shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of YHWH; the water of sprinkling has not been dashed against him: he is unclean.

19:21 And it shall be a perpetual statute to them; and he that sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes; and he that touches the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until evening.

19:22 And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean; and the soul that touches him shall be unclean until evening.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. 4Q27 (4QNumb) is a major witness spanning much of Numbers; its coverage of this specific chapter was not confirmed at verse level from the secondary citations consulted this session. This chapter's ritual is separately discussed at length in later halakhic and sectarian literature (e.g., 4QMMT references purity concerns relevant to this rite), genre-disclosed as interpretive/legal literature, not a running-text witness for this chapter's own base reconstruction.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] This rite's structure -- a female, red, unblemished, never-yoked animal, slaughtered outside the camp and burned whole rather than offered on the altar -- is preserved as a real, disclosed departure from the sacrificial pattern established in Vayikra 1-7, without importing later typological or comparative-religion commentary. Verse 2's אדמה תמימה ("red, faultless") is rendered literally; the precise shade of red intended and the degree of solid coloring required are matters of later interpretive elaboration not specified by MT itself, and this reconstruction does not supply detail beyond what the verse states. The paradox already noted in scholarship -- that the ashes render the one who handles them (vv.7-10, 21) unclean while cleansing the one sprinkled with them -- is preserved exactly as MT presents it without harmonization or explanation.

THE FINAL WILDERNESS YEARS — CHAPTERS 20 THROUGH 25

BAMIDBAR — CHAPTER 20 Miryam's Death — The Waters of Merivah — Aharon's Death

20:1 And the children of Yisra'el, even the whole congregation, came into the wilderness of Tzin in the first month; and the people stayed in Kadesh; and Miryam died there, and was buried there.

20:2 And there was no water for the congregation; and they assembled themselves together against Moshe and against Aharon.

20:3 And the people strove with Moshe, and spoke, saying: Would that we had perished when our brothers perished before YHWH!

20:4 And why have you brought the assembly of YHWH into this wilderness, to die there, we and our cattle?

20:5 And why have you made us come up out of Mitzrayim, to bring us to this evil place? It is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.

20:6 And Moshe and Aharon went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the tent of meeting, and fell upon their faces; and the glory of YHWH appeared to them.

20:7 And YHWH spoke to Moshe, saying:

20:8 Take the staff, and assemble the congregation, you, and Aharon your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it give forth its water; and you shall bring forth to them water out of the rock; so you shall give the congregation and their cattle drink.

20:9 And Moshe took the staff from before YHWH, as he commanded him.

20:10 And Moshe and Aharon gathered the assembly together before the rock, and he said to them: Hear now, you rebels; are we to bring you forth water out of this rock?

20:11 And Moshe lifted up his hand, and struck the rock with his staff twice; and water came forth abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their cattle.

20:12 And YHWH said to Moshe and to Aharon: Because you believed not in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Yisra'el, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.

20:13 These are the waters of Merivah, where the children of Yisra'el strove with YHWH, and he was sanctified in them.

20:14 And Moshe sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: Thus says your brother Yisra'el: You know all the travail that has befallen us;

20:15 how our fathers went down into Mitzrayim, and we dwelt in Mitzrayim a long time; and the Egyptians dealt ill with us, and our fathers;

20:16 and when we cried to YHWH, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and brought us forth out of Mitzrayim; and behold, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your border.

20:17 Let us pass, I pray you, through your land; we will not pass through field or through vineyard, neither will we drink of the water of the wells; we will go along the king's highway, we will not turn aside to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed your border.

20:18 And Edom said to him: You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.

20:19 And the children of Yisra'el said to him: We will go up by the highway; and if we drink of your water, I and my cattle, then will I give the price thereof; let me only pass through on my feet; there is no harm.

20:20 And he said: You shall not pass through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand.

20:21 Thus Edom refused to give Yisra'el passage through his border; therefore Yisra'el turned away from him.

20:22 And they journeyed from Kadesh; and the children of Yisra'el, even the whole congregation, came to mount Hor.

20:23 And YHWH spoke to Moshe and Aharon in mount Hor, by the border of the land of Edom, saying:

20:24 Aharon shall be gathered to his people; for he shall not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Yisra'el, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Merivah.

20:25 Take Aharon and Elazar his son, and bring them up to mount Hor.

20:26 And strip Aharon of his garments, and put them upon Elazar his son; and Aharon shall be gathered to his people, and shall die there.

20:27 And Moshe did as YHWH commanded; and they went up into mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation.

20:28 And Moshe stripped Aharon of his garments, and put them upon Elazar his son; and Aharon died there on the top of the mount; and Moshe and Elazar came down from the mount.

20:29 And when all the congregation saw that Aharon had perished, they wept for Aharon thirty days, even all the house of Yisra'el.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. 4Q27 (4QNumb) is a major witness spanning much of Numbers; its coverage of this specific chapter was not confirmed at verse level from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] A real, disclosed chronological gap: this chapter's events are placed, per the internal dating cross-referenced at Bamidbar 33:36-39 (not yet reconstructed in this project), in the fortieth year after the Exodus, while the narrative material immediately preceding it (chapters 13-19) is dated to the second year -- a gap of approximately thirty-eight years that MT itself does not narrate, consistent with the near-total silence about the intervening wilderness years elsewhere in the Torah. This reconstruction does not supply narrative content for the gap. Verse 12's stated reason for Moshe and Aharon's exclusion from the land ("because you believed not in me, to sanctify me") is rendered exactly as MT states it, without adjudicating between the various interpretive proposals for precisely what their failure consisted of (striking the rock rather than speaking to it, per v.8's instruction; the harsh address to the people in v.10; or some other reading) -- MT itself does not specify which element of vv.8-11 constituted the offense, and this reconstruction does not supply that specification.

BAMIDBAR — CHAPTER 21 The Bronze Serpent — Sichon and Og

21:1 And the Kena'ani, the king of Arad, who dwelt in the South, heard tell that Yisra'el came by the way of Atarim; and he fought against Yisra'el, and took some of them captive.

21:2 And Yisra'el vowed a vow to YHWH, and said: If you will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.

21:3 And YHWH listened to the voice of Yisra'el, and delivered up the Kena'ani; and they utterly destroyed them and their cities; and the name of the place was called Chormah.

21:4 And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way to the Sea of Reeds, to go around the land of Edom; and the soul of the people became impatient because of the way.

21:5 And the people spoke against the Creator, and against Moshe: Why have you brought us up out of Mitzrayim to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, and there is no water; and our soul loathes this light bread.

21:6 And YHWH sent fiery serpents among the people, and they bit the people; and many people of Yisra'el died.

21:7 And the people came to Moshe, and said: We have sinned, because we have spoken against YHWH, and against you; pray to YHWH, that he take away the serpents from us. And Moshe prayed for the people.

21:8 And YHWH said to Moshe: Make for yourself a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole; and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.

21:9 And Moshe made a serpent of bronze, and set it upon the pole; and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked to the serpent of bronze, he lived.

21:10 And the children of Yisra'el journeyed, and pitched in Ovot.

21:11 And they journeyed from Ovot, and pitched at Iyei-Avarim, in the wilderness which is in front of Mo'av, toward the sunrising.

21:12 From there they journeyed, and pitched in the valley of Zered.

21:13 From there they journeyed, and pitched on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness, that comes out of the border of the Emori -- for Arnon is the border of Mo'av, between Mo'av and the Emori;

21:14 wherefore it is said in the book of the Wars of YHWH: Vahev in Sufah, and the valleys of Arnon,

21:15 and the slope of the valleys that inclines toward the seat of Ar, and leans upon the border of Mo'av.

21:16 And from there to Be'er; that is the well of which YHWH said to Moshe: Gather the people together, and I will give them water.

21:17 Then sang Yisra'el this song: Spring up, O well -- sing to it --

21:18 the well, which the princes dug, which the nobles of the people delved, with the scepter, and with their staves. And from the wilderness to Mattanah;

21:19 and from Mattanah to Nachali'el; and from Nachali'el to Bamot;

21:20 and from Bamot to the valley that is in the field of Mo'av, by the top of Pisgah, which looks down upon the desert.

21:21 And Yisra'el sent messengers to Sichon king of the Emori, saying:

21:22 Let me pass through your land; we will not turn aside into field, or into vineyard; we will not drink of the water of the wells; we will go by the king's highway, until we have passed your border.

21:23 And Sichon would not allow Yisra'el to pass through his border; but Sichon gathered all his people together, and went out against Yisra'el into the wilderness, and came to Yahatz; and he fought against Yisra'el.

21:24 And Yisra'el struck him with the edge of the sword, and possessed his land from the Arnon to the Yabok, even to the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon was strong.

21:25 And Yisra'el took all these cities; and Yisra'el dwelt in all the cities of the Emori, in Cheshbon, and in all its towns.

21:26 For Cheshbon was the city of Sichon the king of the Emori, who had fought against the former king of Mo'av, and taken all his land out of his hand, even to the Arnon.

21:27 Wherefore those that speak in parables say: Come to Cheshbon! Let the city of Sichon be built and established!

21:28 For a fire has gone out of Cheshbon, a flame from the city of Sichon; it has devoured Ar of Mo'av, the lords of the high places of Arnon.

21:29 Woe to you, Mo'av! You are undone, O people of Kemosh; he has given his sons as fugitives, and his daughters into captivity, to Sichon king of the Emori.

21:30 We have shot at them -- Cheshbon has perished -- even to Divon, and we have laid waste even to Nofach, which reaches to Meidva.

21:31 Thus Yisra'el dwelt in the land of the Emori.

21:32 And Moshe sent to spy out Ya'zer, and they took its towns, and drove out the Emori that were there.

21:33 And they turned and went up by the way of Bashan; and Og the king of Bashan went out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edre'i.

21:34 And YHWH said to Moshe: Fear him not; for I have delivered him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sichon king of the Emori, who dwelt at Cheshbon.

21:35 So they struck him, and his sons, and all his people, until there was none left him remaining; and they possessed his land.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. 4Q27 (4QNumb) is a major witness spanning much of Numbers; its coverage of this specific chapter was not confirmed at verse level from the secondary citations consulted this session.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verse 14's citation of ספר מלחמות יהוה ("the book of the Wars of YHWH") is a real, significant reference to an external, now-lost source text -- one of several such lost-source citations across the Hebrew Bible (compare the Book of Yashar, cited elsewhere in the Tanakh but not reconstructed in this project). This reconstruction discloses the citation exactly as MT presents it without speculating on the lost work's contents, date, or authorship beyond what this verse itself indicates: that it contained poetic material about place-names along this route. Verse 9's bronze serpent is disclosed without cross-referencing its later reappearance and destruction under Chizkiyahu (2 Melakhim, not reconstructed in this project); this reconstruction addresses only what this chapter itself states. Verses 27-30's embedded victory song ("those that speak in parables") is preserved as a distinct poetic unit within the prose narrative, consistent with MT's own formal shift into verse at this point.

BAMIDBAR — CHAPTER 22 Balak Summons Bil'am — The Donkey Speaks

22:1 And the children of Yisra'el journeyed, and pitched in the plains of Mo'av beyond the Yarden at Yericho.

22:2 And Balak the son of Tzippor saw all that Yisra'el had done to the Emori.

22:3 And Mo'av was sore afraid of the people, because they were many; and Mo'av was overcome with dread because of the children of Yisra'el.

22:4 And Mo'av said to the elders of Midyan: Now will this multitude lick up all that is round about us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field. And Balak the son of Tzippor was king of Mo'av at that time.

22:5 And he sent messengers to Bil'am the son of Be'or, to Petor, which is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying: Behold, there is a people come out from Mitzrayim; behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me.

22:6 Come now therefore, I pray you, curse this people for me; for they are too mighty for me; perhaps I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land; for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.

22:7 And the elders of Mo'av and the elders of Midyan departed with the rewards of divination in their hand; and they came to Bil'am, and spoke to him the words of Balak.

22:8 And he said to them: Lodge here this night, and I will bring you back word, as YHWH may speak to me; and the princes of Mo'av stayed with Bil'am.

22:9 And the Creator came to Bil'am, and said: What men are these with you?

22:10 And Bil'am said to the Creator: Balak the son of Tzippor, king of Mo'av, has sent to me, saying:

22:11 Behold the people that has come out of Mitzrayim, it covers the face of the earth; now, come curse them for me; perhaps I shall be able to fight against them, and shall drive them out.

22:12 And the Creator said to Bil'am: You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people; for they are blessed.

22:13 And Bil'am rose up in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak: Get you into your land; for YHWH refuses to give me leave to go with you.

22:14 And the princes of Mo'av rose up, and they went to Balak, and said: Bil'am refuses to come with us.

22:15 And Balak sent yet again princes, more, and more honorable than they.

22:16 And they came to Bil'am, and said to him: Thus says Balak the son of Tzippor: Let nothing, I pray you, hinder you from coming to me;

22:17 for I will promote you to very great honor, and whatever you say to me I will do; come therefore, I pray you, curse this people for me.

22:18 And Bil'am answered and said to the servants of Balak: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond the word of YHWH my Creator, to do anything, small or great.

22:19 Now therefore, I pray you, stay you also here this night, that I may know what YHWH will speak to me more.

22:20 And the Creator came to Bil'am at night, and said to him: If the men have come to call you, rise up, go with them; but only the word which I speak to you, that shall you do.

22:21 And Bil'am rose up in the morning, and saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Mo'av.

22:22 And the Creator's anger was kindled because he went; and the angel of YHWH placed himself in the way as an adversary against him. Now he was riding upon his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

22:23 And the donkey saw the angel of YHWH standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turned aside out of the way, and went into the field; and Bil'am struck the donkey, to turn her into the way.

22:24 Then the angel of YHWH stood in a hollow way between the vineyards, a fence being on this side, and a fence on that side.

22:25 And the donkey saw the angel of YHWH, and she thrust herself to the wall, and crushed Bil'am's foot against the wall; and he struck her again.

22:26 And the angel of YHWH went further, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left.

22:27 And the donkey saw the angel of YHWH, and she lay down under Bil'am; and Bil'am's anger was kindled, and he struck the donkey with his staff.

22:28 And YHWH opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Bil'am: What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?

22:29 And Bil'am said to the donkey: Because you have mocked me; I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would have killed you.

22:30 And the donkey said to Bil'am: Am I not your donkey, upon which you have ridden all your life long to this day? Was I ever accustomed to do so to you? And he said: No.

22:31 Then YHWH opened the eyes of Bil'am, and he saw the angel of YHWH standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bowed his head, and fell on his face.

22:32 And the angel of YHWH said to him: Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come forth as an adversary, because your way is contrary to me;

22:33 and the donkey saw me, and turned aside before me these three times; unless she had turned aside from me, surely now I would even have slain you, and saved her alive.

22:34 And Bil'am said to the angel of YHWH: I have sinned; for I knew not that you stood in the way against me; now therefore, if it displeases you, I will get me back.

22:35 And the angel of YHWH said to Bil'am: Go with the men; but only the word that I shall speak to you, that you shall speak. So Bil'am went with the princes of Balak.

22:36 And when Balak heard that Bil'am had come, he went out to meet him at Ir-Mo'av, which is on the border of Arnon, which is in the utmost part of the border.

22:37 And Balak said to Bil'am: Did I not earnestly send to you to call you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able indeed to promote you to honor?

22:38 And Bil'am said to Balak: Behold, I have come to you; have I now any power at all to speak anything? The word that the Creator puts in my mouth, that shall I speak.

22:39 And Bil'am went with Balak, and they came to Kiryat-Chutzot.

22:40 And Balak sacrificed oxen and sheep, and sent to Bil'am, and to the princes that were with him.

22:41 And it came to pass in the morning that Balak took Bil'am, and brought him up into Bamot-Ba'al, and he saw from there the utmost part of the people.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] No witness in the standing DSS census produces a confirmed reading specific to this chapter this session. 4Q27 (4QNumb) is a major witness spanning much of Numbers; its coverage of this specific chapter was not confirmed at verse level from the secondary citations consulted this session. Separately, and of major book-level significance disclosed here: the Deir 'Alla plaster inscription (KAI 312), excavated in 1967 at Tell Deir 'Alla in the Jordan Valley, names "Balaam son of Beor... a seer of the gods" as its central figure. VERIFIED by multiple independent, convergent academic and archaeological sources this session: written in a Northwest Semitic dialect distinct from Biblical Hebrew, radiocarbon- and palaeographically-dated to approximately 800 BCE (estimates range c.840-760 BCE), it is a genuine extra-biblical attestation of the name and prophetic role of the figure named in this chapter, discovered outside ancient Israel and independent of the Masoretic transmission. This finding is registered at the book level (apparatus v1.2) given its substantial significance; the primary epigraphic edition (Hoftijzer and van der Kooij, 1976) was not independently consulted this session, this citation resting on convergent secondary academic sourcing. The inscription does not corroborate the specific narrative events of Bamidbar 22-24; it independently attests only that a seer by this name and patronymic was known in the region's own tradition.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] No new evidence beyond the Book-Level Critical Apparatus this session.

[CRITICAL NOTE] Verses 9, 10, 12, 20, and 38's use of the generic term for deity (rendered "the Creator" per the Divine Name Policy) in scenes where a non-Israelite figure receives communication is preserved consistently with this project's standing policy; this reconstruction does not introduce a distinct rendering for Bil'am's own perspective versus the narrator's. The donkey's speech (vv.28-30) is presented without added zoological or folkloric commentary; MT's own matter-of-fact narration of the event, with no signal that the characters find talking livestock remarkable beyond Bil'am's immediate irritation, is preserved as the text's own tone.

BAMIDBAR — CHAPTER 23 Bil'am's First and Second Oracles

23:1 And Bil'am said to Balak: Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.

23:2 And Balak did as Bil'am had spoken; and Balak and Bil'am offered on every altar a bullock and a ram.

23:3 And Bil'am said to Balak: Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go; perhaps YHWH will come to meet me; and whatever he shows me I will tell you. And he went to a bare height.

23:4 And the Creator met Bil'am; and he said to him: I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.

23:5 And YHWH put a word in Bil'am's mouth, and said: Return to Balak, and thus shall you speak.

23:6 And he returned to him, and behold, he stood by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Mo'av.

23:7 And he took up his parable, and said: From Aram Balak brings me, the king of Mo'av from the mountains of the East -- Come, curse Ya'akov for me, and come, execrate Yisra'el.

23:8 How shall I curse, whom the Creator has not cursed? And how shall I execrate, whom YHWH has not execrated?

23:9 For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: behold, it is a people that shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.

23:10 Who has counted the dust of Ya'akov, or numbered the stock of Yisra'el? Let me die the death of the righteous, and let my end be like his!

23:11 And Balak said to Bil'am: What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them altogether.

23:12 And he answered and said: Must I not take heed to speak that which YHWH puts in my mouth?

23:13 And Balak said to him: Come, I pray you, with me to another place, from where you may see them; you shall see but the utmost part of them, and shall not see them all; and curse them for me from there.

23:14 And he took him into the field of Tzofim, to the top of Pisgah, and built seven altars, and offered up a bullock and a ram on every altar.

23:15 And he said to Balak: Stand here by your burnt offering, while I go toward a meeting yonder.

35:16 But if he struck him with an instrument of iron, so that he died, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.

35:26 But if the manslayer shall at any time go beyond the border of his city of refuge, where he fled;

35:27 and the avenger of blood find him outside the border of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood slay the manslayer; there shall be no bloodguiltiness for him;

35:28 because he must remain in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest; but after the death of the high priest the manslayer may return into the land of his possession.

35:29 And these things shall be for a statute of judgment to you throughout your generations in all your dwellings.

35:30 Whoever kills any person, the murderer shall be slain at the mouth of witnesses; but one witness shall not testify against any person that he die.

35:32 And you shall take no ransom for him that has fled to his city of refuge, that he should come again to dwell in the land, until the death of the priest.

35:33 So you shall not pollute the land wherein you are; for blood, it pollutes the land; and no expiation can be made for the land for the blood that is shed therein, but by the blood of him that shed it.
